objectives: Read a connected controlled passage using taught w-CVC patterns.
Identify first, next and last events.
Retell a short passage in logical order.
Use text evidence and rereading to support comprehension and fluency.
concepts: Connected text links individual sentences into a meaningful sequence.
Sequencing tracks events from beginning to end.
A retelling includes the important events in order.
Rereading supports accurate decoding, meaning and fluency.

definitions.definition: The order in which events happen.
To tell the important parts of a text again in order.
Sentences linked together to communicate a complete idea or event.

workedExamples: First Wag can tag; next Wag sits; last Wag rests.
Use first/next/last to retell the passage without changing its events.
Return to the passage when an answer needs text evidence.
commonMistakes: Putting events in a random order.
Adding details not stated in the passage.

basic: Identify first, next and last events in a short controlled passage.
conceptual: Explain how two events are ordered.
application: Retell a controlled passage using sequence language.
higherOrderThinking: Distinguish a text-supported event from an invented detail.
mixedReview: Mix sequencing, decoding, comprehension and fluency.

quickRevision: read → identify events → order them → retell → reread
mistakeBasedRevision: If the order is uncertain, reread each sentence and mark when each event occurs.
weakTopicRevision: Practise ordering three events and retelling them with first, next and last.

activities.name: Retell and reread
steps: Check the retell against the passage.

outcomes: Learner reads a short controlled passage accurately.
Learner sequences three or more stated events.
Learner retells the passage using text-supported events.

questions.question: In the passage, what does Wag do first?
What happens last in the passage?
Which event comes next after Wag tags?
Which detail is stated in the passage?
Put these events in order: tag, sit, rest.
What is the best way to retell the passage?
options: tell the main events in order

questions.question: Why does the learner reread the passage?
Which sentence gives evidence that Wag completed the action?
If Wag tags and then sits, what happened before sitting?
Which retelling is complete?
options: Wag tags, then sits and rests.
